newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Saddam says embargo "marching to its end".
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Saddam says embargo "marching to its end".

text.p: President Saddam Hussein said on Sunday stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Iraq over its 1990 invasion of Kuwait were heading toward their end.

Baghdad radio, in a report on Sunday's cabinet meeting chaired by Saddam, said the Iraqi leader also banned senior government officials from investing in private projects so they would not be swayed by commercial interests.

"The President leader, may God protect him, stressed the embargo is marching to the edge of its end, saying that Iraq's power to face aggression and embargo relies on the ability of the leadership to rally people," the radio said
The six-year U.N. sanctions include a ban on the export of oil and import of all commodities except for food and medicine, which Iraq has little cash to pay for.

Iraq and the United Nations signed a deal in May which would allow Baghdad to export $2 billion of oil over six months to pay for urgently needed food and medicine. The deal was delayed last month after Iraqi military intervention in Kurdish in-fighting.
Washington insists sanctions cannot be completely lifted until Baghdad complies fully with terms of the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire, including scrapping its weapons of mass destruction.
Saddam, quoted by the radio, said that officials of the ruling Baath Party should not set up private businesses or take part in them.

"While the cabinet was discussing some economic issues, the President leader directed that the party and state official should distance himself from establishing private investment projects or taking part in them in order to keep him away from any influence...when he takes a decision," the radio said.
It did not say if the ruling was linked to Baghdad's hopes for the lifting of sanctions.
